title: Evented Stream Endpoint Retirement & Model Alias Consolidation — Client Migration Playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD: Withdraw the legacy evented-stream endpoint and consolidate several model aliases into the unified inference surface. The goal is to reduce maintenance overhead, eliminate duplicated routing logic, and improve telemetry consistency for streaming workloads. This playbook defines scope, rollout phases, acceptance criteria, SDK guidance, and rollback conditions so Engineering and Developer Relations can coordinate low-friction client migrations.
background: Customers currently use two different streaming transports and several model aliases created during rapid prototyping. Maintaining both transports and alias variants increases routing complexity, causes inconsistent latency/cost expectations, and prevents coherent rollout of runtime optimizations (batching + KV cache). Analytics show ~18% of active streaming calls use the evented-stream endpoint and the remaining use the newer unified stream. Several enterprise customers require a migration plan and a minimal-shim compatibility window.
scope_changes: Initial plan removed: keep both endpoints indefinitely. New scope: sunset the evented-stream endpoint for all new customer keys on 2026-06-01 and complete forced deprecation for all keys by 2026-11-01. Consolidate the active aliases: map redwood-chat-v0 and redwood-stream-legacy to unified-chat-1 with documented behaviour differences and compatibility notes.
migration_plan: Phase 0 (Design & Telemetry): define exact behavior differences and instrumentation (Mar 2026).
Phase 1 (Opt-in SDK adapters): ship opt-in client adapters in JS/Python/Go to translate evented-stream calls to unified format (Apr 2026).
Phase 2 (Shadowing & Metrics): enable silent proxying of evented-stream traffic to unified inference in shadow mode and verify parity for 4 weeks (May 2026).
Phase 3 (Soft-roll): reject new evented-stream keys and show deprecation headers; customers with high usage get outreach and migration support (Jun 2026).

Phase 4 (Mandatory Redirect + Fallback Window): automatically redirect remaining evented-stream calls to unified endpoint while providing structured error details for incompatible payloads (Sep 2026).
Phase 5 (Enforced Retirement): fully remove evented-stream transport and alias mappings from routing layer (Nov 2026).
rollout_phases: Canary: apply the redirect for 5% of internal traffic and two low-risk customers; evaluate latency and output diffs.
Staged customers: invite customers with <5k monthly streaming tokens to opt-in migration with SDK help.
Enterprise migration: schedule migration windows and runbooks with Customer Success for customers requiring bespoke mapping rules.
Public deprecation: announce global date, provide CLI migration assistant and one-click SDK upgrade guide.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: <0.5% output regression (semantic divergence) measured across 3 representative prompt suites after shadowing period.
Performance: median p95 latency change <= +12ms for streaming calls in canary buckets.
SDK adoption: official JS/Python/Go adapters downloaded and enabled by at least 30% of migrated early adopters in first month.
Compatibility: automatic redirect handles 98% of evented-stream payloads without user code changes; remaining cases documented with clear remediation steps.
Operational: Alerting and dashboards for migration-related errors in Console are available and linked from the rollout playbook.
telemetry_gates: Shadow parity gate: semantic-diff rate <0.5% over 2 consecutive weeks in shadow traffic.
Error-rate gate: increased application error rate in canary traffic must remain <0.2% above baseline or rollout pauses.
Cost gate: per-token cost delta for redirected traffic must be within +/-10% of the original routing profile.
compatibility_shim: We will provide a runtime shim for 6 months that accepts the evented-stream framing and forwards messages to the unified endpoint while emitting deprecation headers. The shim will reject patterns that depend on legacy SSE reconnection semantics; these will be surfaced as structured migration errors with suggested code patches.
sdk_guidance: Publish adapter packages: @redwood/stream-adapter, redwood_stream_adapter, redwood-stream-adapter-go with opt-in enable flags.
Provide migration snippets: show minimal diffs for reconnect handling, streaming chunk assembly, and finalization frames.
Testing harness: include a reproducible test harness and sample prompt sets that customers can run against their CI to assert parity before switching.
Backward compat: adapters must optionally emit legacy telemetry tags so customers can align their internal dashboards during migration.
customer_communications: Initial notice: targeted emails and Console banner to customers using evented-stream with >1k monthly tokens (Apr 2026).
Migration guide: step-by-step doc with code samples, expected incompatibilities, and a checklist (May 2026).
Office hours: weekly migration office hours hosted by DevRel and Solutions Eng for 12 weeks post-announcement.
Final reminder: 60/30/7 day countdown notices and an auto-schedule option for assisted migration.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: High-volume customers rely on legacy reconnection semantics. Mitigation: Offer a limited extended-support window and a paid migration engineering engagement.
Risk: Output regressions for certain prompt patterns. Mitigation: Build targeted regression suites and require manual sign-off from Research for affected models before full enforcement.
Risk: SDK fragmentation. Mitigation: Provide canonical adapters and collaborate with major OSS clients to upstream fixes.
